build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player recruits gladiators from a market by spending gold. Each gladiator has combat stats (strength, speed, defense), a weapon preference, and a crowd appeal rating. Recruited gladiators join the roster. Score 0 if gladiators cannot be recruited, if they have no stats, or if recruitment is free.

Gladiators are trained between fights by assigning training regimens. Training improves stats over time but costs gold. Different regimens improve different stats. Score 0 if training does not exist, if it has no stat effect, or if it is free.

Fight nights are scheduled and the player picks matchups. Fights play out automatically based on gladiator stats. The crowd reacts to dramatic moments. Winners earn prize gold; losers may be injured or killed. Score 0 if fights cannot be scheduled, if combat has no resolution, or if there are no consequences.

A gold economy drives the arena: revenue from ticket sales and sponsors, expenses from recruitment, training, upkeep, and medical bills. A gold counter is permanently visible. Score 0 if there is no gold system or if income and expenses are absent.

The full loop connects: title -> new season -> recruit/train/schedule -> fight night -> results -> next week. The game tracks arena prestige and season wins. A season end shows final results. Score 0 if any transition is missing or if there is no season structure.

At least four gladiator types exist with different weapon styles (sword/shield, trident/net, dual blades, heavy mace) affecting combat behavior and crowd appeal. Score 0 if all gladiators fight identically or if fewer than three styles exist.

Training regimens (strength drills, sparring, showmanship) have different effects on different stats. The player must choose which stats to prioritize for each gladiator. Score 0 if only one training type exists or if all training is identical.

Opponents vary in difficulty and style. Visiting challengers and rival arena fighters have different stats and fighting approaches. Later season opponents are stronger. Score 0 if all opponents are identical or if difficulty does not escalate.

Arena prestige grows with exciting fights and famous gladiators, attracting bigger crowds and richer sponsors. Prestige is tracked and affects revenue. Score 0 if prestige does not exist or if it has no effect on income.

Betting allows the player to wager gold on fight outcomes for extra profit. Upsets can occur, making betting a genuine risk/reward decision. Score 0 if betting does not exist or if outcomes are predetermined.

The HUD shows gold, arena prestige, roster summary, and calendar/schedule in clear non-overlapping regions. During fights, gladiator HP and crowd excitement are visible. Score 0 if gold, prestige, or fight state is missing.

The arena compound view shows training grounds, barracks, and arena floor as distinct areas. During fights, gladiators and the crowd are visible. Management and combat screens are clearly different. Score 0 if areas are indistinguishable or if fights have no visual arena.

Actions produce visible feedback: recruiting shows gladiator join roster, training shows stat changes, fights show combat with hits and reactions, crowd excitement builds visibly, and injuries/deaths are shown. Score 0 if actions produce no observable change.

Overall art coherence: arena, gladiators, crowd, training grounds, and UI belong to a consistent Roman-fantasy visual language with sand-and-steel grandeur. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles or reads as plain default plain grey. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Gladiator sprites are real illustrated or pixel-art warriors with distinct weapon styles and armor. Different types have unique silhouettes. Score 0 if gladiators are plain colored shapes.
The arena floor uses real textured sand with blood stains and weapon marks. The surrounding colosseum has illustrated architecture with crowd seating. Score 0 if the arena is a flat colored area.

HUD and UI use styled themed widgets with Roman chrome: gladiator cards have scroll/tablet styling, gold displays have coin motifs, and menus have stone-and-iron backgrounds. Score 0 if UI elements are unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults.

Animation and atmosphere: gladiators fight with attack animations, crowd cheers and reacts, training shows movement, blood/sparks fly during combat, and the arena has ambient atmosphere (torch flicker, dust motes). Score 0 if all elements are static.
